about: Labeled corpus of ROUGE-1 residual-ASCII hazards for non-Latin text, pinned to the documented default tokenizer in google-research/rouge (tokenize.py) and the count-based ROUGE-N scoring in rouge_scorer.py. Each 'expected' value is hand-traced from the tokenizer and reproduced by test_rouge1.py (stdlib only). Chinese glosses are provided; strings use real characters.
tokenizer: lowercase; re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', text); re.split(r'\s+', text); keep tokens matching r'^[a-z0-9]+$'; default use_stemmer=False so no stemmer is applied

cases.note: Both sentences collapse to the single residual ASCII token '2024'; ROUGE-1 reports a perfect match between opposite claims.
A correct summary that omits the year has no surviving ASCII token and scores 0.
A wrong summary that happens to share the year scores 1.0, outranking the correct one above.
Both strings tokenize to empty; this is the already-documented zero-ROUGE phenomenon, included for contrast.

cases.prediction_gloss: the same number with a thousands separator
cases.note: ASCII-only, language-independent: a comma splits one number into two tokens so an identical value scores 0.
